# Reload action is lost after a pane returns from the edge rail

## Context

Found by lived use of the Workstation on `dev@0659b0e42d` (2026-09-01, first session on the rebuilt v13.2 DockLayouts) while exercising the default action rail that landed through `#18014`. A pane that goes through the auto-hide round trip (unpin → rail → reveal → Pin) comes back into flow **without its `reload` header action**. Every other engine action survives the trip.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues (created-desc) at 2026-09-01T19:58:43Z, the last 30 A2A messages (all read-states) at 19:59Z, and the Knowledge Base ticket corpus; no equivalent. The nearest open dock defects are `#18027` (maximize FLIP arming) and `#18029` (native-titlebar popup drag) — different surfaces.

> **Body update 2026-09-01T21:00Z (author):** implementing this surfaced a second, independent mechanism behind the same symptom — the reveal pane / flow pane id collision below. One symptom, one gesture, one PR; the ticket body carries both so the ACs stay coherent.

## The Problem

Reproducer (Chromium, `apps/workstation`, fresh load, both readings taken from the DOM through the header toolbar's action `aria-label`s):

1. Click the **Queues** tab header. Actions on the header: `reload`, `unpin`, `pop out`, `maximize`, `close`.
2. Click `unpin` → the pane collapses onto the left rail. Click the rail tab → the reveal overlay opens. Click its `Pin` → the pane returns into flow at its original position.
3. Click the **Queues** tab header again. Actions: `unpin`, `pop out`, `maximize`, `close`. **`reload` is gone** — not focus-gated (`neo-toolbar-action-context-inactive`), but absent from the DOM, i.e. the action instance sits at `hidden: true`.

Control: **100k Matrix**, which never railed, keeps its `reload` (context-inactive while unfocused, offered on focus) across the same sequence.

The user-facing cost is the one the default rail was built to remove: a pane that was reloadable a second ago silently is not, with no state change the user can see. The Workstation has no `dockReload()` implementations, so every pane's reload is served by the engine recreate fallback (`#17966` / PR #17996) — the action should be offered on every returned pane.

## The Architectural Reality

### Mechanism 1 — the post-settle sweep walks the OLD shell's tabs

- `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs` projects the engine `reload` action with a **constant** `hidden: true` — deliberately: a row that varies between projections replaces the action group mid-reconcile, which the stable-instance rule forbids. Availability rides the retained instance's runtime state through `Workspace#syncDockReloadAction` (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2283`), which un-hides it whenever an active item resolves and either the pane carries `dockReload()` or `hasDockRecreateFallback()` holds.
- That sync runs post-settle from `Workspace#refreshDockWorkspace` — twice, both times as `syncDockHeaderActions(result?.currentTabs)` (`Workspace.mjs:3372`, `:3379`).
- `result.currentTabs` is the reconciler's map of the **old** shell's tabs: `Reconciler.collectProjectedTabs(oldShell)` (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/Reconciler.mjs:204` for the stable path, `:403` for the staged transaction), returned unchanged at `:257` / `:512`.
- `syncDockHeaderActions` (`Workspace.mjs:1726`) walks the settled shell itself **only when the handed map is empty** (the fresh-boot case). A non-empty map that lacks a node is taken at face value.
- A railed item projects no tabs node while `autoHidden`; pinning it back creates a **fresh** tabs node in the next shell. That node is not in `currentTabs`, the map is non-empty (every other node was retained), so the fallback walk never fires and the fresh node's `reload` stays at its projected `hidden: true`.
- `Workspace#onDockActiveIndexChange` would rescue it on the next activation change — but a single-tab node never sees one, and a single-tab edge pane is exactly the shape of every Workstation edge pane.
- `close`, `pin`, `lock`, `pop-out` derive their `hidden` from the projection context at projection time, so they are right on a fresh node without any sync. `reload` is the one action whose availability rides the post-settle sync by design, and it is the one that is lost.

This is the Workstation's mechanism: measured with the shell walk in place, the Workstation's returned pane offers `reload` again. A unit witness reproduces it in isolation (a recreate-fallback workspace, an edge item committed `autoHidden`, `setItemPinned` through the reducer: the retained node's reload is synced, the fresh node's is not).

### Mechanism 2 — the reveal pane and the flow pane collide on one id

Every dock component fixture (and any consumer whose `resolvePane` returns a **config with a deterministic `id`**) hits a second failure on the same gesture, measured on the `dock-maximize` fixture with a temporary refresh trace:

- `Workspace#resolveRevealPane` defaults to `resolvePane`, so the rail's reveal overlay materializes its own pane from the same config (`Rail#syncRevealPane`, cached in `revealPaneCache`, **parked** on dismissal — removed from the slot without destroy, keeping a stale `parentId`).
- The pin escape commits `setItemPinned(true)` and schedules the refresh; the refresh mints the flow pane from the same config → `manager.Base: Trying to create an item with an already existing id`.
- The staged transaction then tears the OLD rail down, whose `destroy()` destroys its cached reveal pane → the shared id is **unregistered under the live flow pane** → the old shell's own teardown walks a vdom that still references that id → `util.VDom.getVdom: Component not found for id: …` → the refresh **rejects**, silently (`refreshPromise` tails are `.catch(() => {})`-ed), so neither post-settle sweep runs — and the flow pane is an unaddressable zombie.
- Corollary found on the way: releasing the parked pane *inside* the refresh, while the dismissal's own slot update is still in flight, hangs the reconcile (a `promiseUpdate` that never settles). The reveal pane has to leave **through its slot, in the dismissal's own update**, ahead of the refresh.

## The Fix

1. **Sweep coverage (mechanism 1):** `Workspace#syncDockHeaderActions()` walks the SETTLED shell, always; the reconciler's map is no longer consulted (the parameter goes away — its only truthful meaning was "old shell", which is exactly the wrong set). Every write in the sync stays change-guarded, so re-walking retained nodes is idempotent. No projection-time availability for `reload` — the stable-instance rule stays.
2. **Reveal-pane release (mechanism 2):**
   - `Rail#releaseRevealPane(itemId, silent=false)` — destroys and forgets a cached (blueprint/placeholder-created) reveal pane; through its slot while the slot still lists it, directly when parked. Live instances are never cached, so a consumer's own pane cannot be reached.
   - The rail releases on its own leave paths **before** the dismissal parks the pane: the pin escape (`onRevealPinRequested`) and a reconciled leaver (`reconcileTabs`). One update retires the DOM node and the registration together, ahead of the refresh that mints the flow pane.
   - `Workspace#releaseStaleRevealPanes(document)` — a silent pre-projection sweep in `refreshDockWorkspace` for the leave paths that never pass through a rail (a restored perspective, a transfer), which take the staged path that tears the old rail down only after the new shell minted the flow pane. Shares one `forEachDockRail` walker with `syncDockLockRails`.
3. **Red-first arms:** a component arm on the `dock-maximize` fixture (`pinned` gains the reload contract; unpin → rail reveal → Pin → the returned node offers `reload`, focus-gated), a unit witness for the sweep gap, a unit witness for the id collision (a fixed-id workspace: the flow pane takes the id, is alive and registered, the reveal pane was released, the refresh settled, the sweep ran), and a rail witness for `releaseRevealPane` (cached pane destroyed and forgotten; pin escape releases through the slot; live instance untouched).

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace#syncDockHeaderActions()` | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1726` | syncs every tabs node of the settled shell; no map parameter | no settled shell → no-op (unchanged) | method JSDoc | unit witness + component arm |
| `reload` availability after the rail round trip | `Workspace.mjs:2283` + `LayoutAdapter.mjs` engine header set | offered on the returned pane exactly as on a never-railed one | unchanged (`hidden` when neither `dockReload()` nor the recreate fallback can serve the item) | none | component arm |
| `Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.Rail#releaseRevealPane(itemId, silent)` | new, `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Rail.mjs` | destroys + forgets a cached reveal pane of an item leaving auto-hidden state; live instances unreachable | no cached pane → no-op | method JSDoc | rail unit witness |
| `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace#releaseStaleRevealPanes(document)` | new, `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` | silent pre-projection release for leave paths outside the rail | no rails → no-op | method JSDoc | workspace unit witness |
| reveal-state retirement on the sweep path | `RevealStateMachine` contract table (`itemCleared` on pin, restore, transfer, policy) | the sweep calls `revealMachine.itemCleared(itemId)` after releasing the pane, so the machine is idle and the overlay's `revealPaneItemId` is cleared for a departed item | no machine (destroyed rail) → no-op | `releaseStaleRevealPanes` JSDoc | workspace unit witness + `DockLock` component arm |

**Decision Record impact:** aligned-with ADR 0029 §2.7 (the auto-hide contract: reveal → pin restores the pane into flow with nothing lost). No amendment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A component arm drives unpin → rail reveal → Pin on the `dock-maximize` fixture and asserts the returned node's header exposes `reload` as a focus-gated action; it fails on current `dev` (received 0 reload nodes) and passes with the fix.
- [ ] A unit witness reproduces mechanism 1: after the pin-back refresh, the retained node's reload is synced and the fresh node's is un-hidden too.
- [ ] A unit witness reproduces mechanism 2: with a fixed-id `resolvePane`, the pin escape returns the pane to flow with the flow pane alive and the only registered holder of the id, the reveal pane released, `refreshPromise` settled, and the sweep run.
- [ ] A rail witness: `releaseRevealPane` destroys and forgets a cached pane, the pin escape releases through the slot (slot empty, id free), a live instance is never cached.
- [ ] The never-railed control keeps its behavior; the existing dock component specs (`DockReload`, `DockLock`, `DockMaximize`, `DockPopOut`, `DockBootSweep`, `DockRailTabPaint`) and the dashboard unit folder stay green.
- [ ] No second write path: no projection-time availability for `reload`, no sync inside the reconcile's own update train.
- [ ] The Workstation reproducer above is re-run by hand at the PR head and the returned pane offers `reload`.

## Out of Scope

- The reveal header's own actions and the rail preview surface (`#18028`, merged).
- Reload semantics and the recreate fallback (`#17948`, `#17966`, both merged).
- Maximize arming order (`#18027`) and the native-titlebar popup drag path (`#18029`).
- The narrow-header title collapse under a five-action rail (a design decision, filed separately if the operator wants it).
- Surfacing a rejected refresh: `refreshPromise` tails swallow rejections by design (the chain must stay alive), which is why mechanism 2 was invisible. Worth its own leaf — a rejected refresh should at least log.

## Avoided Traps

- **Deriving `reload`'s `hidden` at projection time** — it would fix mechanism 1 and reintroduce the mid-reconcile action-group replacement the LayoutAdapter comment forbids.
- **Syncing beside the projection application** — the bar write racing the refresh's own update train is the collision that duplicated retained chrome on slow rigs (`Workspace.mjs:3365`); the fix stays in the post-settle slot.
- **Treating the reconciler's `currentTabs` as "all tabs"** — its name is honest; the bug is the consumer assuming otherwise.
- **Releasing the reveal pane inside the refresh only** — a parked pane whose dismissal update is still in flight cannot be destroyed under the reconcile without hanging it; the rail releases on its own leave paths first, the workspace sweep is the silent backstop.
- **Handing the reveal pane to the flow instead** — tempting object permanence, but `resolveRevealPane` is a documented override point ("a reveal must render differently from the tab flow"), so the reveal pane is not always the flow pane.
